newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Mozart classic abducted in cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: Mozart classic abducted in cyberspace.

text.p: A young Austrian opera production which had its premiere on Wednesday night is testing the limits of Salzburg's prestigious music festival.

The annual event in Mozart's city of birth, which gives a major focus to the composer, has extended its traditional repertoire into cyberspace with a radically redesigned version of "The Abduction from the Seraglio".
On a stage piled with TV and computer monitors, the real world meets the virtual as singers serenade projected images.
The show begins with a bang, blasting the audience with computerised information to convey the initial scenario.
While surfing the Internet, three friends mysteriously disappear, leaving behind their distraught companion, Belmonte.
An e-mail gives a hint as to their whereabouts. They have been captured in a powerful computer system that threatens to eradicate their human existence.
Not only a daunting set up for hero Belmonte, who begins a virtual search for his beloved Konstanze and her entourage, the avant-garde work is a challenge to true Mozart fans.

Every note of the score has been digitally modulated or electronically produced, leaving only the arias untouched. These are sung live on stage by a young ensemble, to digitalised music played from a hard disc.
"I don't have a problem with the computerised sound", commented a member of the audience after the performance. "But it must be hell for the singers".
Basic computer literacy is required to follow the action. Video projections from a central work station suggest a multi-faceted digital prison, constantly teasing with images of the abducted trio.

In the original plot, the three friends are kept captive in a Turkish palace, an exotic scenario much en vogue in late 18th century Europe. Transposed into the age of cyberspace, Internet replaces Orient. Belmonte's task is to invade the computer network jealously monitored by Osmin the web master.

Sneaking in via a home page, Belmonte manages to acquire the digital tools necessary to navigate through the system. Together with his captured companian, Pedrillo, he programmes an escape route for his friends.
The reunited couples attempt a break out. Donning virtual reality head gear, they frantically veer around the stage in fairground bumper cars.
But it is only when the almighty system, Bassa Selim, makes his decision to let the lovers go, that the simulated world around them dissolves.

Mozart's popular opera classic as a giant computer game? This innovative production, which has found the support of the director of the Salzburg Festival, Gerard Mortier, demonstrates one thing for certain. However modified, it is still Mozart's musical genius that provides the ultimate thrill of the evening.
The six week festival comes to a close on the last day of August.
